purpose.is: Turns the owner's build-mode rule from a note in an agent's memory into a flag the system reads: one record, on or off, with an expiry the system enforces, a card id, and a scope.

While the flag is on, old-line gates, hooks, guards, leases, watches and status rules are not rendered into rebuild seats (N-13), and a refusal that names an old rule is recorded as rule.bit and does not stop the ticket (factory-rebuild-plan.xml failure case governance-interference).
purpose.is-not: It is not a bypass of the gate: coq/gate on the head sha (N-08, N-25) and the reviewer record (N-19) still decide a merge under build mode. It is not a lift of permissions for the owner's break glass, which is N-42's one-time control.action.
purpose.why: L11 F1: build mode is a note, not a mechanism, and an agent switching rules off by hand is the pattern the owner rejected the same day. herdr/config/exemptions.json already has the right shape: rule, until, card_id, why (L11 section 8).

input.record: A ruling record whose body names flag build-mode, state on or off, scope (rebuild or all), expires_at in UTC, and the card id or chat relay id it came from. Re-entry from N-32 (page) or N-42 (Controls screen control.action, re-entered through N-29).
The scheduler tick; on every tick the node compares now with the live expiry.

output.record: The flag as the system now holds it: on or off, scope, expires_at, card id, the ruling id, and a reason (ruling, expired, start-reconcile).
A ruling refused: same card id already applied, expiry in the past, expiry beyond the configured maximum, or a scope not in the table.
output.reads: N-13 (renders the seat bundle with the old-line layer off when on and the ticket is in scope), N-42 (Controls screen lamp and the control to turn it off early), N-28 (one card when the flag expires with rebuild tickets still open), N-51 (the exit test records the flag state of the day).

mechanism.where: Go package flags inside the service; one row per flag name in the flags table, with version for compare-and-swap. build-mode is the first flag; hold (N-42) is the second and uses the same package.
mechanism.step: On a ruling record with body.flag = build-mode: validate (expires_at after now; expires_at minus now at most flags.build_mode.max_duration from config, default P7D; scope in {rebuild, all}; card_id not already applied).
Put build-mode.state 200 with expected version = live version. On 409 from the store, re-read and re-validate once; a second 409 is reported as build-mode.state 409 with reason race.
On every tick: if the live state is on and now is at or after expires_at, put build-mode.state 200 off with reason expired, by the system, card_id of the ruling it closes.
On unit.start: run step 3 once before the first dispatch, so a flag that expired while the service was down is cleared before any seat renders.

When the flag turns off by expiry and N-03 reports rebuild tickets still open (ticket.waiting or ready with scope rebuild), emit one owner-acts record (build-mode.state 200 off with open_rebuild_tickets greater than 0); N-28 turns it into one card with the recommendation to extend or to let the rules apply.
mechanism.scope: Scope rebuild applies to tickets whose body.lane is rebuild (cut from this spec book by N-17 and N-18); scope all applies to every ticket. A ticket's scope is fixed at cut and read by N-13 from the dispatch record.

diagram.mermaid: stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> off off --> on : ruling on (card id, expiry) CAS ok on --> on : ruling on with later expiry (extend) CAS ok on --> off : ruling off on --> off : tick at or after expires_at (system) off --> off : expired-at-start reconcile (unit.start)

effects.effect: With the flag on and the ticket in scope, the seat bundle omits every hook, guard and watch from the old line (compaction-guard binding, nudge, trust writer, idle watch, prettier PostToolUse, AutoMem) and renders settings from the role only; the bundle hash records build_mode=true.

A failure record whose reason names an old rule (a refusal string in the old-rule table of shared/principles.xml#build-mode) is written as rule.bit 300 with the rule name, and the attempt is not counted against the ticket's three; the ticket is re-dispatched; a fix ticket request for the rule goes to N-03 once per rule name.
rule.bit is not a card; the ledger and the Stats screen show it. The expiry-with-open-tickets record is one card.
The Controls screen shows the lamp (on, scope, time left) and offers turn off now as a control.action that re-enters at N-29.
None. The gate, the reviewer record and the machine merge apply under build mode; a rule that blocks a rebuild ticket is a defect in the rule, a failing test is not.

start.s: The ruling arrives as a record from N-29 (the owner's card answer, a chat relay recorded by the system lane, or a Controls screen action). No agent edits a flag file; no seat reads a memory note.
Expiry is enforced by the tick (N-06) and reconciled at unit start; no one has to remember to turn it off.

wait.fallback: one re-read and retry; then build-mode.state 409 reason race; the live state is unchanged and the next tick re-evaluates
the system turns it off and posts one card if rebuild tickets remain open

wait.what: N-03 open-ticket count for the expiry card
wait.fallback: post the card with count unknown rather than skip it

waits.cog-test: The cog that could stall this node is a human remembering to turn build mode off. The expiry removes that cog; the owner's only action is optional (extend early).

retries.recover: After three failures the node writes build-mode.state 409 with the reason and leaves the live state; nothing else waits on it, because readers read the live state, not the attempt.
retries.report: A ruling refused for an expiry beyond the maximum is reported back to the page as the card's answer status (N-29 re-asks with the maximum stated); never silently clipped.

many-agents.readers: Twenty seats rendering at once read the flag from the dispatch record N-07 gave them (N-07 copies the live state and its version into dispatch), so a flip during a render cannot split one seat's bundle between two states.
many-agents.writers: Only the service writes build-mode.state; every write is compare-and-swap on the flag row's version; rulings are applied in store sequence order, so two rulings in the same second resolve deterministically and the later one wins.
many-agents.collision: The same card answered twice (page retry, chat relay plus page): the second ruling with the same card_id is refused 409 duplicate; the first stands.

An expiry tick and an extend ruling at the same moment: both CAS on the same version; one wins; the loser re-reads. If extend won, the flag is on with the later expiry; if expiry won, the extend applies on its retry as a fresh on with its own expiry, and the two records show the order.
A seat whose bundle was rendered under on while the flag turned off keeps its bundle for that run (one-shot, D02); the next attempt renders under the new state.

status-codes.emits: State applied (on, off, expired); system acts; when body.open_rebuild_tickets is greater than 0 on an expiry, the owner acts through one card.
Ruling refused (duplicate card, bad expiry, bad scope, race); N-29 acts by re-asking with the reason.
Written by N-11 on this node's rule; listed here because the flag defines when it may be written.

state-paths.path: Flag transitions as log lines; the store is the truth.
state-paths.rule: herdr/config/exemptions.json is not written by this node; it is a source and is retired with the herdr config tree by N-49 once N-13 renders bundles from the flag.

edges.out: build-mode.state (through the dispatch record of N-07)

item.check: A ruling turns the flag on with its expiry and card id.
item.proof: A test ruling, then one build-mode.state 200 on with the same card_id and expires_at.

item.check: The system turns it off at expiry without any ruling.
item.proof: Fake clock advanced past expires_at; one build-mode.state 200 off reason expired by N-44.

item.check: An expired flag is cleared at unit start.
item.proof: Store seeded with an expired on; unit start; off record before the first dispatch record.

item.check: A duplicate card id is refused.
item.proof: Second ruling with the same card_id; build-mode.state 409 reason duplicate; live state unchanged.

item.check: N-13 renders a bundle without old-line hooks when on and in scope.
item.proof: N-13 test: bundle settings.json has no hooks key and build_mode true in the bundle hash input.

item.check: A rule refusal under build mode does not count an attempt.
item.proof: N-11 test: failure record naming an old rule; rule.bit 300 written; the ticket's attempt counter unchanged; one fix ticket request.

may.do: turn the flag on or off through a card, the Controls screen or a recorded chat relay
apply rulings, expire the flag, write build-mode.state and rule.bit

may-not.do: write build-mode.state, rule.bit or any flag; read the flag from anywhere but its dispatch record
turn the flag on by editing a file, a memory note or a config

monitoring.counter: Time to expiry; an alert record at one hour left while rebuild tickets are open.
How often each old rule bit; the top rule is the next fix ticket.
monitoring.lamp: Lit while on, with scope and time left; the turn-off control beside it.

step.when: a rebuild ticket is refused by an old rule

runbook.step: Nothing by hand. Read the rule.bit record and the fix ticket request; the ticket re-dispatched on its own.
Answer the card: extend (a new ruling with a new expiry) or let the rules apply.
A ruling is recorded by the system lane from the owner's chat words (N-29 relay path); never by editing the store.
runbook.cold-start: The flag row is in the store; unit start reconciles expiry; nothing else to restore.

sources.source: Principle build-mode: old rules off for rebuild tickets, nodes ship dark, a blocking rule is a defect, the ledger records which rule bit
Case governance-interference: proceed, cut the fix ticket, record which rule bit
D13 B: build mode as a flag with an expiry that the gates read, the shape of herdr/config/exemptions.json

reject.source: herdr/config/exemptions.json as the live flag file
reject.reason: A file an agent edits is a hand step and lives in the repository; the flag is a store record with a ruling behind it. The file's shape is kept, its role is not.
An open-ended exemption is how the old rules stayed half-on; the owner's D13 ruling names the expiry.

reject.source: build mode lifting the gate or the reviewer
reject.reason: The owner's statement is about old governance rules, not tests; D15 keeps the machine verdict for every merge.
Dead enforcement files referenced by no settings (L11 section 9); under build mode and the repo-owned seat layer they are not loaded; N-49 disposes of them.

shared-needs.need: principles.xml#build-mode with the old-rule table: every old-line rule name and the refusal string it prints, so N-11 can match a refusal to a rule.
flags: name, state, scope, expires_at, card_id, ruling_id, version; unique on name.
ruling (body.flag, state, scope, expires_at, card_id), build-mode.state, rule.bit, ticket.request (fix ticket for a rule).
300 for rule.bit (routed, informational, nobody acts), 409 duplicate ruling (N-29 acts).
A seat bundle under build mode: which layers are omitted; the bundle hash input includes build_mode and scope.
The dispatch record copies build-mode.state and its version.
